**Finding: Compliant (at fallback) — no redline proposed.**

Clause 4(a) (¶p0016) is the operative termination-for-convenience provision, and it lands on the playbook's fallback position:

| Element | Document | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Committed term | 1 year Initial Term, auto-renewing 1-year terms | Not multi-year → no "missing behaviour" deviation |
| AP convenience right | Any reason, 90 days' notice, after Initial Term | Fallback: 60–90 days ✓ |
| Early-termination fee | None | Fallback cap: ≤3 months ✓ |
| Kubient convenience right | Any reason, 90 days' notice, not during Initial Term | Walk-away is <90 days → not triggered |

Two points worth noting on the economics: AP pays no fees under clause 5 (¶p0023) — the revenue share runs from Kubient to AP — so there are no prepaid fees needing a pro-rata refund, and Kubient's entitlement to "all fees generated during the termination period" is just its continuing share of impressions actually monetised while it is still serving, not an exit penalty or acceleration.

Two sub-elements fall short of the *preferred* position but, per the classification rules, are recorded in the rationale rather than flagged: AP's notice is 90 days rather than 30, and Kubient's convenience right is not expressly limited to the end of a renewal term. Flag for the deal team: if the term is ever extended beyond one year, or renewal terms lengthened, this clause should be reopened to add a 30-day AP right with a refund mechanic.
